BB,SB, BR - Mon., Nov. 16, 2026 and Tues., Nov 17, 2026.

Failure to notify PROCOM may result in the next highest ranked contestant being contacted and offered the position. If a contestant chooses not to be accepted as an entry at the San Antonio Rodeo due to injury or any other reason, the next highest ranked contestant from the Qualifying performances will be contacted and offered the position. This procedure will be followed until all available positions are filled. These contestants (or teams) will be randomly placed among the other contestants (or teams) that have already been accepted for the San Antonio Rodeo. If ties in the average result in more contestants (or teams) to advance to the San Antonio rodeo than there are positions available, the tied contestant(s) with the single highest score or fastest time at the qualifying rodeo will advance. If still tied, the contestant(s) with the highest ranking in the 2026 PRCA World Standings will advance.
RE - Riding stock for the Qualifying performance will be drawn at least 24 hours prior to the performance.

RE - Three re-rides will be available (and on site) for each performance for each of the riding events. In addition, three more re-rides will be designated to be used, "only if needed", in the case that one or more of the three originally designated re-rides are used to replace a sick or injured animal that was drawn by a contestant. If in the event that more re-rides are awarded that there are re-ride animals available, additional re-rides will be drawn from animals in that pen.

RE- If an animal has already been drawn for a contestant who turned out, the replacement contestant will draw an animal from a pool consisting of all animals that have been notified as turned out through PROCOM (includes D.R's and V.I.R's) and the 1st available designated re-ride.
BR - Day money will be paid for each day of slack.
TD - There will be a disqualification for a jerk down as long as all criteria are in compliance with the jerk down policy

TD: Thursday, November 19 at 9 AM. One go-round. Top 20 in the long go advance to the qualifying rodeo performances on Friday, November 20 and Saturday, November 21. Payoff will be accordance to the rulebook. Stock charge $30 per contestant.

SW: Thursday, November 19 at 12 PM. One go-round. Top 20 in the long go advance to qualifying rodeo performances on Friday, November 20 and Saturday, November 21. Payoff will be in accordance with the rulebook. Stock charge $30 per contestant.

TR: Tuesday, November 17 at 3 PM. One go-round. Top 20 in the long go will advance to the qualifying rodeo performances on Friday, November 20 and Saturday, November 21. Contestants must rope with the same partner for both go-rounds. Payoff will be accordance with the rulebook. Stock charge $15 per contestant.

TE - If a tie results in more than 20 to advance to the performances on Friday, November 20 and Saturday, November 21 the contestant with the highest ranking based on 2026 World standings will advance. In the TR, the team with the single partner with the highest ranking based on 2026 World standings will advance.
TE - If a timed event animal escapes (or a re-run is due for any other reason), the extra will be used. Only escaped animals go back into the herd.

ALL EVENTS - The San Antonio Stock Show & Rodeo Qualifier and the San Antonio Stock Show & Rodeo will each count as separate rodeos. All entries are official unless contestant specifies otherwise at time of entry.
PAYOFF: $5,000 added purse plus entry fees. Pay-off will be in accordance with the rulebook for one go-round plus a progressive round.
ALL EVENTS - Money will be divided equally in case of splits and any odd pennies will be dropped.

ALL EVENTS - if not enough contestants or teams qualify for the number of places to be paid in an event, the remaining places shall be divided evenly among those contestants or teams who did qualify (have a score or time), and that money will be considered ground money and will not be posted as Championship Points, and will not count towards qualifying for the National Finals Rodeo (except in the bull riding).

If a header or heeler qualifies in both categories (2026 money won and champion at one of the 7 rodeos) he will assume the position among the 2026 money won qualifiers. The 56 headers who qualify must rope with the 56 heelers who qualify. If a contestants' partner is drawn out due to qualification, the contestant who qualified will not be allowed to draw out. Contestants who do not have partners after the contestant list has been determined will be allowed to designate partners during the extended grace period on Mon., Dec. 21 between 10 AM and 4 PM. After the expiration of the grace period, a random draw by PROCOM will determine which headers who are not entered with a partner will rope with which heelers who are not entered with a partner. If a header or heeler notifies a TO, WIR, DR, or DO prior to the 30-hour deadline, leaving an incomplete team, the next contestant in the corresponding category (header or heeler) on the alternate list of contestants that were drawn out due to qualification, will be added to the team (any TO, VIR, or DO notification made through PROCOM will be final). If a notification is not made prior to the 30-hour deadline, the remaining partner may select another partner from among any of the PRCA event contestants already entered at the rodeo, except those scheduled to compete in the TR. No partners can be replaced after a team has competed in round 1 of each bracket. In the event that one or more of the listed qualifier rodeos is canceled for any reason during the 2026 rodeo season, the next highest ranked contestant on the alternate list based on 2026 money won will be accepted.

ALL EVENTS - If first place at one of the seven qualifying rodeos is tied and none of the tied contestants are already qualified among the top 48 from 2026 money won, the tied contestant with the highest ranking based on 2026 money won will be accepted. If there is a tie in the Team Roping for first place at one of the seven qualifying rodeos, the highest ranked header and the highest ranked heeler from the tied teams based on 2026 money won will be accepted.
BR - No sharp spurs. Judges will inspect spurs prior to the first go-round of each bracket.
BB, SB, BR - Any contestant awarded a re-ride option and whose equipment is broken must immediately repair and/or find replacement equipment.
RE - Riding event stock will be drawn after the trade deadline the night before the respective bracket. All trades must be confirmed prior to the stock draw for the first go-round of each bracket.

RE - Two re-rides will be available (and on site) for each round for each of the riding events. In addition, two more re-rides will be designated to be used "only if needed", in the case that one or more of the two originally designated re-rides are used to replace a sick or injured animal that was drawn by a contestant. If in the event that more re-rides are awarded than there are re-ride animals available, additional re-rides will be drawn from animals in the re-ride pool.
RE - Riding event pens and re-ride orders to be set by FWSSR producer. Rodeo producer will consult with RE representatives when selecting RE stock.
TE - Stock contractor to provide one animal for every entry, plus adequate extras.

SW - The steer must fall, clean when the throw is attempted. If a clean fall is not achieved, and the motion stops, the steer must be allowed to regain his feet before being thrown. If the steer is not allowed to regain his feet when instructed by the judge, the contestant will be disqualified.
TE - If a timed event animal escapes or a re-run is awarded for any reason, the extra will be used. Only escaped animals go back into the herd.
TD - There will be a disqualification for a jerk down as long as all criteria are in compliance with the jerk down policy.

BB, SB, BR-If an individual is taking advantage of the contestants in that event and/or the livestock and/or the rodeo production and/or not cooperating with the chute boss's and judges' instructions resulting in an attempt to cheat or influence the results of the event, to include but not limited to causing an animal to act up or be unruly in the chute in order to receive a re1ide, that individual will be disqualified by the judges from that round and for subsequent offenses will be disqualified by the judges from that event for the remainder of the rodeo.

For contestants, the definition of "ready when called" shall be: BB: The contestant must be over the horse with his hand in the rigging when the previous horse leaves the arena. If the contestant is first to compete, this would be when the flag horse leaves the arena or as instructed by the chute boss and/or judges. If a contestant has a fair opportunity to compete and does not call for his competition animal, delaying the production of the rodeo, the same ruling will apply.

SB: The contestant must have the horse cinched (front & rear) with the rein measured, and be in the chute, mounting the horse when the previous horse leaves the arena. If the contestant is first to compete, this would be when the flag horse leaves the arena or as instructed by the chute boss and/or judges. If a contestant has a fair opportunity to compete and does not call for his competition animal, delaying the production of the rodeo, the same ruling will apply.

BR: The contestant must be pulling the rope when the previous bull leaves the arena. If the contestant is first to compete, this would be when the flag horse leaves the arena or as instructed by the chute boss and/or judges. If a contestant has a fair opportunity to compete and does not call for his competition animal, delaying the production of the rodeo, the same ruling will apply.

A contestant not ready when called during a performance or section of slack will be fined $250 for the first offense; $500 for the second offense; and $1,000 for the third and subsequent offenses, and/or may be disqualified from the rodeo.

TE - If in the opinion of the chute boss and/or the judges, if a contestant is not "ready when called" the contestant will be subject to a penalty. By definition, "ready when called" shall mean that the contestant must be riding into the box when the previous animal leaves the arena. If a contestant is the first contestant in team roping and tie-down roping, they shall be riding into the box, and in steer wrestling, riding into the arena when the flag (sponsor) horse leaves the arena or as instructed by the chute boss and/or judges. Contestants must take their stock within 45 seconds of receiving the "all clear" from the designated judge. If the contestant exceeds the time limit, except in case of mechanical failure or a problem with the competition animal in the timed event chute in the opinion of the judges. For every 20 seconds over the 45-second limit, the fine will be progressively doubled. If a contestant exceeds two minutes in the box it will result in disqualification from the round. A contestant not ready when called during a performance or section of slack will be fined $250 for the first offense; $500 for the second offense; and $1000 for the third and subsequent offenses, and/or may be disqualified from the rodeo.
ALL EVENTS - If a re-ride or re-run is awarded for any reason, it may take place before the next event.
ALL EVENTS - Once the run or ride has been completed, contestants must promptly exit the arena.
ALL CONTESTANTS - Must compete in all brackets and rounds in order to advance to the wild card, semi-finals and/or finals ( does not include DR's or VIR's or 2nd go-round replacements).

FORMAT - All events. 18 total performances - 7 brackets of eight (8) contestants or teams competing in 2 rounds back to back each will account for the first 14 performances, 1 Wild Card Round for performance 15, 2 Semi-Finals for performances 16 and 17 and 1 Finals Round for performance 18. The top 2 money winners (14 total) in each bracket will advance to compete in one of the semi-finals performances (8 contestants or teams per performance). The third top money winner from each bracket (7 total) will advance to the Wild Card Round which will also consist of one round. The remaining non-qualifiers from each bracket that did not advance will be placed into a pool of non-qualifiers. At the conclusion of bracket 7, the top money winner from the pool of non-qualifiers will advance to the Wild Card Round to fill the number 8 position in that round. The top two money winners from the Wild Card Round will advance to one of the semi-finals performances. No previous times or scores will be carried forward. The qualifiers for the two semi-finals performances will be seeded as follows: Semi-Finals number one (performance 16): #1 money winners including ground money from brackets 1, 3, 5, 7 and the #2 money winners from brackets 2, 4, 6 and the Wild Card round. Semi-Finals number two (performance 17): #1 money winners including ground money from brackets 2, 4, 6 and the Wild Card round, and the #2 money winners from 1, 3, 5, and 7. The actual competition order will be drawn randomly. Qualifying contestants or teams will have until 30 minutes following the end of the 7th bracket to trade. Wild Card qualifiers will have 30 minutes after that performance to trade. No previous times or scores will be carried forward. From the semi-finals, the top 4 contestants or teams per performance based on fastest times and highest scores will advance to the finals (8 total). the finals (performance 18) will consist of 8 contestants or teams. The event champion will be determined by the highest score or fastest time in the finals. No previous times or scores will be carried forward.

TIES - For advancement purposes only. If there is a tie in the bracket, Wild Card, or Semi-Finals, it will be broken by any single fastest time or highest score in any round in the bracket. If still tied, the tie will be broken by any round winner in the bracket. If still tied, the tie will be broken based on the highest amount of money earned in the previous year's PRCA World Standings. If there is a tie in the Finals for event champion, co-champions will be awarded. Ties for pay-out will be treated as such and split evenly among the tied contestants or teams in all brackets and rounds.

REPLACEMENTS: ALL EVENTS - If a contestant who is entered in any of the brackets turns-out (includes DR's and VIR's) through PROCOM prior to, during or after their first competition performance, the position will be filled with the next qualified alternate.** All non-notified turnouts will be replaced with the next available contestant.** If a contestant who advances to the Wild Card turns-out (includes DR's and VIR's), the contestant that has the next highest earnings at the Fort Worth Stock Show & Rodeo in that respective bracket will be placed in the available position in the Wild Card (drop down until filled). If a contestant who has qualified for the semi-finals turns-out (includes DR's and VIR's), the contestant with the next highest score or fastest time from the Wild Card will advance to semi-finals (drop down until filled). If a contestant who advances from the semi-finals to the finals turns-out (includes DR's and VIR's), the contestant that has the next fastest time or highest score in the semi-finals will be placed in the available position in the finals (drop down until filled).

ALL EVENTS - If not enough contestants or teams record a qualifying time or score to fill the available positions from the brackets to the Wild Card round and/or Semi-Finals round, the available positions will be filled using the following criteria: most money won in the brackets, if still unable to fill, fastest time or highest score in the brackets, if still unable to fill, the available positions will be filled based on the highest amount of money earned in the previous year's PRCA World Standings. If not enough contestants or teams record a qualifying time or score to fill the available positions from the Wild Card round to the Semi-Finals round, contestants or teams from the Wild Card round will advance based on the following criteria: most money won in the brackets if still unable to fill, fastest time or highest score in the brackets, if still unable to fill, the available positions will be filled based on the highest amount of money earned in the previous year's PRCA World Standings. If not enough contestants or teams record a qualified time or score to fill the available positions from the Semi-Finals round to the Final round, contestants or teams from the Semi-Finals round will advance based on the following criteria: next qualified time or score in any performance of the Semi-Finals, if unable to fill, the contestant in the Semi-Finals with the most money won in the brackets, if still unable to fill, the contestant in the Semi-Finals with the fastest time or highest score in the brackets, if still unable to fill, the available positions will be filled based on the contestant in the Semi-Finals with the highest amount of money earned in the previous year's PRCA World Standings. ALL EVENTS: A contestant can draw and compete on an animal in the Semi-finals, the Wild Card Round, or the Finals that he previously competed on in his respective bracket.
ALL EVENTS - Any money won shall not count for Texas Circuit Standings or as a Texas Circuit participation count towards qualification for the Texas Circuit Finals Rodeo.

PAY-OFF - All events. No average. Pay-off for each round within the brackets: 1st - $2,500 (per man in TR), 2nd - $1,800 (per man in TR), 3rd - $1,500(per man in TR), 4th $1,000 (per man in TR), 5th through 8th $125 (per man in TR). Pay-off for the 15th performance (Wild Card round): 1st - $2,500 (per man in TR), 2nd - $1,800 (per man in TR), 3rd $1,500 (per man in TR), 4th - $1,000 (per man in TR). Pay-off for the 16th and 17th performances (Semi-Finals rounds): 1st - $4,700 (per man in TR), 2nd - $3,600 (per man in TR), 3rd - $2,600 (per man in TR), 4th - $1,600 (per man in TR). Pay-off for the 18th performance (Finals round): 1st - $20,000 (per man in TR), 2nd $12,000 (per man in TR), 3rd - $8,000 (per man in TR), 4th - $4,000 (per man in TR).

ALL EVENTS - For the first 17 performances, if not enough contestants or teams qualify for the number of places to be paid in an event, the remaining places shall be divided evenly among those contestants or teams who did qualify (have a score or time), and that money will be considered ground money and will not be posted as Championship Points, and will not count towards qualifying for the National Finals Rodeo (except in the bull riding). In the finals, if there are not four qualified rides or times, the remaining placings will be paid out on the highest scores or fastest times in the Semi-Finals and all money paid out will count for championship points.
ALL EVENTS - Money will be divided equally in case of splits and any odd pennies will be dropped.

ALL CONTESTANTS - No entry, including contestants with back numbers, will be granted into the Rodeo arena beginning 1 hour prior to each round, no exceptions. All stock inspections must be performed in the arena pen area or timed event staging area. Contestant back numbers must be visible at all times to gain entry into the bucking chutes, timed event staging areas, arena alleys/ staging area, rodeo arena and the Dickies Arena floor level. If the contestant is wearing a jacket or vest, the contestant back number must be pinned on the out of the jacket or vest, or the jacket or vest must be removed.

ALL EVENTS - Each contestant must complete a W-9 and submit the completed form to FWSSR officials prior to the contestant's first competition. FWSSR officials will not authorize payment of prize money to any contestant who does not have a valid W-9 on file with the FWSSR.

ALL CONTESTANTS - The "walk-up replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information section of the business journal.

GRACE PERIOD - Will expire one hour after entries close.
QUALIFICATIONS: 40 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. 20% top circuit, 80% top money. No exemptions.

FORMAT - One go-round with 8 contestants advancing to a finals. For the first go-round, there will be four sections with 10 contestants competing in each section. The top two contestants from each section based on highest scores will advance to the finals for a total of 8 contestants in the finals (will not exceed 8). If ties result in more than two within a section to advance, a random draw by the judges will determine which of the tied contestants will advance. If there are less than two qualified rides within a section, the contestant with the next highest score from the other sections will advance. If tied, a random draw by the judges will determine which of the tied contestants will advance. The stock contractor will set the four sections of horses. All 40 contestants will draw at all 40 horses and the contestants will compete in the section in which their drawn animals have already been placed. The competition order for the finals will be determined by random draw. The order of the draw will be the same as the competition order.

PAY-OFF: 6% of the total amount (added money plus entry fees) will be deducted prior to the pay-off for the PRCA. Of the remaining amount, 60% will be allocated to the first go-round (15% to each of the four sections), and 40% will be allocated to the finals. Each section will pay two places (60% for first place and 40% for second place). The finals will pay four places. Any ties in the sections or the finals will be paid in accordance with the PRCA rulebook.
ALL CONTESTANTS - A contestant will not be accepted as an entry at an X-Broncs Event if he is already placed in a position at another PRCA rodeo or event on the same day as the X-Broncs Event.
